Session.title: Session
Session.description: Represents a single session within the leadership seminar.

time.description: The time slot of the session (e.g., '9:00 AM - 10:00 AM').

title.description: The title of the session (e.g., 'Understanding the Vision of the Church').

speakerId.description: Reference to the Speaker entity. (Relationship: Speaker 1:N Session)

content.description: The duration of the content portion of the session in minutes.

qa.description: The duration of the Q&A portion of the session in minutes.

prayer.description: The duration of the prayer portion of the session in minutes.

afternoon.description: Indicates whether the session takes place in the afternoon.

summary.description: A short summary of the session's content.

Speaker.title: Speaker
Speaker.description: Represents a speaker at the leadership seminar.

name.description: The name of the speaker (e.g., 'Bishop Davis Freeman').

title.description: The title or credentials of the speaker (e.g., 'Dr.', 'Bishop').

definition.description: Stores session information. The 'sessionId' parameter is the unique identifier for each session.
Stores speaker information. The 'speakerId' parameter is the unique identifier for each speaker.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to store session and speaker data for the leadership seminar application. Since there is no user-specific data or collaborative aspects involved, we will use simple collections at the root level. This approach simplifies data management and security rules.

To ensure Authorization Independence (Strategy A), there is no need for denormalization as all data is treated equally and accessible to everyone. 

To enable secure list operations (QAPs), structural segregation (Strategy B) is not required as the data does not need access controls.

As there is no role-based access control, DBAC is not applicable.
